text:
marco: Heads-up — starting account/project + VPC scaffold for the new SAO2 region (Brazil). Need a quick preflight on GPU quota, CIDR plan, and egress/NAT pattern before I land the TF modules.

alex: 👍 can you drop the current CIDR sketch and intended GPU pool sizes? want to check overlap with existing peered VPCs.

marco: Sketch: reserved 10.52.0.0/16 as region umbrella. Plan GPU subnets as /20s per AZ: 10.52.16.0/20 (gpu-a), 10.52.32.0/20 (gpu-b), 10.52.48.0/20 (gpu-c). Shared services + infra: 10.52.0.0/22, apps: 10.52.4.0/22, dbs: 10.52.8.0/22.

sylvie: That seems OK but watch for /20 fragmentation if customers request large private pools later. Suggest reserving an extra /20 as buffer (10.52.64.0/20).

jess: GPU quota — we need at least 64 A100-equivalent GPUs to start. Cloud quota request usually takes 48–72h in BR. Have we opened the support ticket?

marco: Not yet. I can open the quota ticket but need the exact SKU mix (A100/RTX8000) and vCPU/accelerator limits. Any preferences?

alex: Start with mix: 32x A100-80GB + 32x A10G (or cheaper Ampere cards) to allow variable batches. Also request regional vCPU bump: +1024 vCPUs. Include placement groups if provider supports.

infra-bot: Reminder: for new region, enable organization-level service APIs and attach Organization Policy:compute.disableSerialPortAccess=false, billing export configured. See: https://infra.redwood/internal/runbooks/region-onboard

ops-oncall: NAT/egress pattern: prefer centralized managed NAT gateway in one AZ + autoscaling SNAT pool. If we do SNAT per subnet we'll run out of ephemeral ports quickly with large batch clients.

marco: Noted. Plan: centralized NAT with private egress via managed bastion for admin. For GCP we will set up Cloud NAT with minPortsPerVm bump. For AWS use NAT Gateway + EIP pool.

alex: Quick validation commands before TF apply (run from infra-admin):
```bash
# GCP: check project APIs and quotas
gcloud services list --enabled --project=redwood-sao2
gcloud compute project-info describe --project=redwood-sao2 | grep -i quotas

# AWS: verify VPC CIDR availability (simple check)
aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=cidr,Values=10.52.0.0/16 || true
```

sylvie: Also run a simple IP overlap check against peering map (I uploaded CSV to /shared/netmaps/sao2_peers.csv). Small Python check: 
```python
# quick overlap check
from ipaddress import ip_network
ours = ip_network('10.52.0.0/16')
peers = [ip_network(x.strip()) for x in open('sao2_peers.csv')]
for p in peers:
    if p.overlaps(ours):
        print('OVERLAP', p)
```

jess: On cost: reserve a portion as savings plan / commitment to lock A100 price? or start on on-demand and move to committed once steady-state? Initial 64 GPUs on-demand will spike billing.

alex: If we expect 3 months steady usage, commit for at least 25–50% via reserved instances/savings plan to reduce unit cost. Tagging must be in place to link usage to cost center.

marco: Action items I’ll take: 1) open quota ticket with SKU counts + vCPU bump, 2) land TF module PR for VPC + subnets + Cloud NAT, 3) add extra /20 buffer, 4) run overlap check, 5) schedule handoff meeting with security for KMS and peering.

jess: I can own the savings-plan analysis once we have expected burn by week 2.

infra-bot: CI note: include `infra/terraform/modules/vpc/sao2` in the plan run to validate resources. Use workspace `sao2-prod`.

ops-oncall: If quota request is delayed >72h, fallback: spin smaller dedicated capacity in a nearby region (GIG or SFO) and route via cross-region traffic until quota approved. Keep me posted.

marco: Opening ticket now and will paste the SR number here. Thx all. :rocket:
